close_reason:
Superseded by bd:JMAP-1j9k.9 (closed by commit b6d2ebb on 2026-05-17). Same closure reasoning as the blocking dep JMAP-tjvm.16: the workspace adopted the OPPOSITE policy. Public method-input Params structs in *-client crates do NOT use #[non_exhaustive]; forward-compat for future spec-defined fields is the flatten-ed 'extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' field per workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy.

Adding #[non_exhaustive] to MetadataGetParams, MetadataSetParams, MetadataQueryParams, MetadataQueryChangesParams (or MetadataChangesParams from the sibling wzq9.15) would now be the regression — those structs already follow the workspace-canonical shape: a single pub 'extra' flatten field with #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]. Verified in crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/methods/mod.rs:36-167 (all 5 structs carry the extra field; default serialization produces {}; vendor-extras propagate on the wire; round-trip tests at lines 561-642 cover this).

The bead's own agent-authored recommendation was correct at the time of filing (2026-05-15) but the workspace policy decision rolled the opposite way two days later. The forward-compat path is: add a new typed field on the struct as a new minor version (the struct-literal syntax break the bead describes is real, but the workspace decision was that the extras flatten field is sufficient forward-compat for vendor / site fields, and that typed-field addition warrants a struct-literal break by design — see the policy note in workspace AGENTS.md and the design-decision comment at calendars-client mod.rs:108).

Sibling wzq9.15 (MetadataChangesParams) is currently 'blocked' on the same now-defunct JMAP-tjvm.16 dependency and falls under the identical policy reversal — flagged for separate closure pass.
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:36-48 (MetadataGetParams), :58-71 (MetadataSetParams), :125-138 (MetadataQueryParams), :146-159 (MetadataQueryChangesParams) — all four params structs are declared as:

    #[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct MetadataXxxParams { pub extra: serde_json::Map<…> }

Missing #[non_exhaustive]. Each currently carries a single pub extra field, but a caller can use struct-literal syntax:

    MetadataGetParams { extra: serde_json::Map::new() }

When a future draft revision adds a typed method-level arg (e.g. forAccount, or any new typed knob the draft has not yet committed to), every caller using struct-literal syntax breaks at compile-time, requiring a major version bump.

wzq9.15 already calls out MetadataChangesParams (the one struct with non-extras typed fields) and notes workspace-wide divergence from extras-preservation policy. But wzq9.15's title and explicit-mention naming covers only MetadataChangesParams. A fix-author closing wzq9.15 could plausibly add #[non_exhaustive] to MetadataChangesParams alone and consider the ticket done — leaving the other 4 metadata-client params structs unprotected at 0.1.0.

This finding exists to make the scope explicit: all 5 params structs in this crate need #[non_exhaustive] simultaneously, and the fix propagates from canonical mail-client per the canonical-template propagation rule (see wzq9.15's blocking dep on JMAP-tjvm.16).

Trigger: any future draft-or-vendor-defined typed method-level arg.
Fix: add #[non_exhaustive] to MetadataGetParams, MetadataSetParams, MetadataQueryParams, MetadataQueryChangesParams (alongside MetadataChangesParams from wzq9.15).

Cross-ref: wzq9.15, JMAP-tjvm.16.
title: Params structs missing #[non_exhaustive]: MetadataGet/Set/Query/QueryChanges (extends wzq9.15)
